words.meaning: Not showing or known by name; without a known identity.
words.example: The prize money was donated by an anonymous well-wisher who didn't want any credit.

words.meaning: Uncomfortable, clumsy, or embarrassing to be in or watch.
words.example: There was an awkward silence after he forgot the punchline of his own joke.

words.meaning: Very strange or unusual, almost shocking.
words.example: It was bizarre to see snow falling in the middle of summer.

words.meaning: A line that marks the limit or edge of an area or topic.
words.example: The fence marks the boundary between our garden and the neighbor's.

words.meaning: To happen at the same time as something else.
words.example: Her birthday happens to coincide with the school's sports day this year.

words.meaning: To begin or start.
words.example: The ceremony will commence as soon as the principal arrives.

words.meaning: To fully understand something.
words.example: It took me a second reading to fully comprehend the complicated instructions.

words.meaning: To hide something carefully so it cannot be seen.
words.example: He tried to conceal his nervousness by smiling throughout the interview.

words.meaning: To face a difficult person or problem directly.
words.example: She finally decided to confront her fear of public speaking.

words.meaning: To say the opposite of what someone else has said.
words.example: His excuse seemed to contradict what he had told the teacher the day before.

words.meaning: To communicate or make an idea or feeling known.
words.example: The poster's bright colors convey a sense of excitement about the festival.

words.meaning: To work together with others toward the same goal.
words.example: The two rival teams had to cooperate to finish the science project on time.

words.meaning: To match or be similar to something else.
words.example: The numbers on the map correspond to the list of landmarks below it.

words.meaning: To want something very strongly.
words.example: After the long hike, everyone began to crave a cold glass of water.

words.meaning: Exactly correct, with no mistakes.
words.example: Her description of the accident was so accurate that the police had no questions.

words.meaning: To state something firmly and confidently.
words.example: He calmly asserted his opinion during the debate, even though others disagreed.

words.meaning: Empty or bare; unable to produce plants, crops, or life.
words.example: After years of drought, the once-green fields became barren and dusty.

words.meaning: To accept something as true without checking first.
words.example: Don't assume the store is closed just because the lights are off.

words.meaning: To settle a disagreement by each side giving up part of what it wants.
words.example: The siblings reached a compromise and agreed to share the last slice of cake.

words.meaning: To make something known that was previously secret.
words.example: The company had to disclose the results of the safety test to the public.
